The brief spike in power consumption when some devices are turned on is due to a phenomenon called inrush current. Inrush current is the excess consumption caused by the inductance and capacitance that the circuit has. Transformers and motors (inductance) can consume a very high amount of current when initially connected to power. This can be over 10 times the normal operating current, but the spike is short lived. Capacitors (capacitance) can also draw high current when initially charging up then settle down to operating current. The behavior you describe on your TV sounds like the capacitors in the switch mode power supply are the cause of the inrush current spike. It's normal and so short that it should no be a considerable factor in the overall power consumption. There are many more variables at play in an electronic/electrical circuit so things get complicated quickly, such as why your well pump motor has a non-linear power consumption rate on two different voltages/phases. That's a bigger discussion and not really relevant to OP's question anyway.
